logline: Washington D.C. crisis manager Olivia Pope fixes everyone else's scandals while her own life - entangled with the President and a shadow intelligence operation - becomes the biggest crisis she cannot solve.

renewal.note: Seven seasons concluded on ABC on April 19, 2018. Creator Shonda Rhimes announced the final season in advance, allowing a planned conclusion.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 earned 87% on Rotten Tomatoes from 31 critics. Joshua Alston at Vulture called it 'a solid appetizer that lays a solid foundation for Olivia's future.' Sarah Hughes at the Guardian found it 'simultaneously brilliant and crazy.'

pull_quotes.text: Season one is a solid appetizer that lays a foundation for Olivia's future and delivers one of the show's greatest finale twists.

seasons.review_body: Scandal's compressed seven-episode first season arrived in April 2012 and earned 87% on Rotten Tomatoes from 31 critics. Joshua Alston at Vulture described it as 'a solid appetizer that lays a solid foundation for Olivia's future, and it delivers one of the show's greatest finale twists.' Sarah Hughes at the Guardian noted it 'hurtles towards a climax that is simultaneously brilliant and crazy.' Kerry Washington's Olivia Pope - rapid-fire, imperious, and privately unravelling - was identified immediately as a rare creation: a network drama lead whose intelligence and authority were the premise rather than the aspiration. Alan Sepinwall at HitFix noted after four episodes that the show's world-building remained murky.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 scored 95% on Rotten Tomatoes. Alan Sepinwall at HitFix reversed his Season 1 reservations: 'It's ludicrous on virtually every level; it's also an enormous amount of fun, thanks to the writing and the performances.'

pull_quotes.text: It's ludicrous on virtually every level; it's also an enormous amount of fun, thanks to the writing and the performances.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 is where Scandal made its case as essential television, earning 95% on Rotten Tomatoes and transforming the show from a press qualifier into a genuine cultural phenomenon. Shonda Rhimes threw out any hesitation about the show's soap-opera register and committed fully: the twists were operatic, the pacing was relentless, and the emotional manipulation was deliberate and precise. Alan Sepinwall, who had been cautious in Season 1, reversed course entirely: 'It's ludicrous on virtually every level; it's also an enormous amount of fun, thanks to the writing and the performances.' The live-tweet audience for Scandal became one of the defining social media events of the era.
seasons.season_over_season: The leap from Season 1 to Season 2 is one of television's sharpest mid-series accelerations - the show finds its gear and never looks back.

bollymeter.basis: Season 4 achieved a perfect 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, the series' peak. Ryan McGee at The A.V. Club argued Scandal was the show the future of television 'should be aiming to actually produce.'

pull_quotes.text: Scandal is the show those looking toward television's future should be aiming to actually produce.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 is Scandal's critical apex: a perfect 100% on Rotten Tomatoes and the series' most frequently cited run of episodes. Ryan McGee at The A.V. Club wrote that it demonstrated the show's capacity to give audiences 'what they want, and then giving them so much more than they ever expected' - calling Scandal 'the show those looking toward the future of television should be aiming to actually produce.' The season's B613 conspiracy arc gave the show its most dramatically ambitious material, while individual episodes achieved a tonal range - from courtroom procedural to political thriller to genuine emotional devastation - that few network dramas of the era matched.
seasons.season_over_season: The creative peak - Season 4's perfect Rotten Tomatoes score marks the point where Scandal is operating at network television's highest level.

episode_reviews.title: The Lawn Chair
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: One of the most praised Scandal episodes ever aired, this standalone story about a Black father standing guard over his son's body after a police shooting transcended the show's usual genre registers to become something closer to social document. Kerry Washington and Courtney B. Vance anchored an hour that operated outside the show's mythology entirely.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A father's vigil over his son's body becoming a standoff with law enforcement - the episode doing with dramatic television what documentary footage could not.

critic_note.text: Scandal is the show those looking toward television's future should be aiming to actually produce.

bollymeter.basis: The final season scored 92% on Rotten Tomatoes - strong but below peak seasons. The Shonda Rhimes-planned conclusion gave the writing room to wind down arcs rather than simply dropping them.

seasons.review_body: Scandal's seventh and final season aired from October 2017 to April 2018, earning 92% on Rotten Tomatoes. The Shonda Rhimes-announced planned conclusion gave the writing room to wind down arcs rather than simply dropping them, and the press appreciated the attempt at a coherent ending for a show that had accumulated extraordinary narrative complexity. The season's Olivia-Pope-as-power arc gave Kerry Washington the most morally unambiguous dramatic material of the run. The overall Metacritic series score of 66 (based on 33 critics from the debut season) significantly understated the show's trajectory - Scandal improved substantially season-on-season from that modest opening benchmark.
seasons.season_over_season: A more measured wind-down than the show's explosive middle seasons, but the planned ending structure gives the finale more dignity than most Shondaland endgames.
